sec: Athero-embolic renal disease: lab investigations & treatment · p804

items.q: Match the lab investigations of athero-embolic renal disease — 1) Complement  2) Eosinophils  3) WBC count  4) S. Amylase … A) ↑  B) Hypocomplementemia (↓C3, ↓C4)  C) Eosinophilia  D) Eosinophiluria with Hansel's stain
items.exp: Lab investigations in athero-embolic renal disease: hypocomplementemia (↓C3, ↓C4); eosinophilia; eosinophiluria with Hansel's stain; ↑WBC count; ↑S. amylase. (Book p804)

items.q: Eosinophiluria in athero-embolic renal disease is demonstrated with:
items.exp: Lab investigations: eosinophiluria with Hansel's stain, along with eosinophilia, hypocomplementemia, ↑WBC count and ↑S. amylase. (Book p804)

items.q: A patient with suspected athero-embolic renal disease has raised amylase but no abdominal pain. What does this indicate?
opts: ↑S. amylase is a listed lab feature, reflecting pancreatic/mesenteric involvement
Acute pancreatitis is the primary diagnosis
items.exp: Lab investigations in athero-embolic renal disease include ↑S. amylase (along with mesenteric ischemia in the clinical features). (Book p804)

items.q: If the diagnosis of athero-embolic renal disease is in doubt, biopsy should be taken from:
items.exp: Biopsy (if in doubt) of skin — never kidney — in athero-embolic renal disease. (Book p804)

items.q: In suspected athero-embolic renal disease, skin biopsy is preferred and renal biopsy is avoided.
opts: True — 'biopsy (if in doubt) of skin, never kidney'
False — renal biopsy is the investigation of choice
False — both kidney and skin should be biopsied together
True, but only if complement is low
items.exp: The book states: biopsy (if in doubt) of skin (never kidney) — avoiding renal biopsy in a disease with multiple small-vessel occlusion and poor prognosis. (Book p804)

items.q: The biopsy figure in athero-embolic renal disease shows birefringent, biconvex, elongated cholesterol crystals. These are seen in:
opts: Small vessels, causing multiple small vessel occlusion
items.exp: The figure is labelled 'birefringent, biconvex elongated cholesterol crystals' — the embolic material that occludes small vessels in athero-embolic renal disease. (Book p804)

items.q: Fill up: The cholesterol crystals of athero-embolic renal disease are described as birefringent, biconvex and ______.
items.exp: Skin/lesion biopsy shows birefringent, biconvex, elongated cholesterol crystals (figure). (Book p804)

items.q: The treatment specified for athero-embolic renal disease on this page is:
items.exp: Treatment: ACE (–) — ACE inhibitors are avoided in athero-embolic renal disease (as in renal artery stenosis). (Book p804)

items.q: All but one of the following are lab features of athero-embolic renal disease. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Athero-embolic renal disease produces hypocomplementemia (↓C3, ↓C4), eosinophilia, eosinophiluria with Hansel's stain, ↑WBC count and ↑S. amylase. (Book p804)
